requested.title: A `</script` substring in a rune module silently disables the whole oxc dropped-call scan for that file
Subsetting silently deletes an @font-face when its unicode-range list is not in ascending order
Previous HMR artifact is unlinked before the in-flight import() of it has resolved
Hardcoded `tailwind-rebuild` handler name makes a second setupTailwind() call silently disable the first stylesheet's dev watcher

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: Confirmed end-to-end by reading Svelte 5.57.3's own parser. `scriptPrograms()` (oxcDroppedCalls.ts:85-87) wraps a non-`.svelte` source in `<script module lang="ts">…</script>` and hands it to `parse()`. In `svelte/src/compiler/phases/1-parse/read/script.js:11,25`, `regex_closing_script_tag = /<\/script\s*>/` is fed to `Parser.read_until_regex` (1-parse/index.js:282-298), which returns the slice up to the **first** match in the remaining template. So any complete `</script>` sequence in the developer's own module — in a string, template literal, or comment — truncates the wrapped text at that point. The call path to real user modules is real: `registerSvelteModuleLoader` (clientBuildLoaders.ts:54-62) registers `onLoad({ filter: /\.svelte\.[jt]s$/ })` and passes `original` (the untranspiled author source) to `onCompiled`, which ComponentRegistry.ts:1331 binds to `warnOxcDroppedCalls` → `findOxcDroppedCalls` (line 684-685). The truncated text then either fails acorn (swallowed by the `catch` at lines 102-105, whose comment — 'the compiler reports the real syntax error' — is wrong here, since the real file compiles fine) or, when the truncation lands in a comment, parses as a valid but empty/partial Program. Either way the function returns no findings, so every `$effect`/`$derived.by` in that file goes unscanned and a silently non-reactive effect ships with no warning — which is the entire purpose of this diagnostic (`oxcDroppedCalls.test.ts:247-255` proves rune modules are a first-class scan target via the `tracker.svelte.ts` fixture). One imprecision in the write-up: truncation requires the full `</script>` (the regex demands the `>`), not a bare `</script` substring; the concrete example given satisfies this. The suggested 8-for-8-char replacement (`</script` → `<!script`) does preserve every AST offset and the `line` computation at line 120. The secondary observation that `visit()` (lines 107-145) sits outside the try/catch, unlike the deliberately-wrapped sibling diagnostic (ComponentRegistry.ts:1964-1989, 'must never break a build'), is structurally accurate, though I found no realistic throw path there — callee/identifier names are the only regex inputs and are escaped. Correctness/DX only, as the finding itself states: the input is the developer's own source, so there is no attacker-controlled surface. BUG is the right severity.

Verified by tracing both inputs to `intersectRanges` and every consumer of the result. `intersectRanges` (fontImportAttributes.ts:189-206) is the textbook two-pointer interval-list intersection: it advances `i` or `j` purely on `a[i].hi < b[j].hi`, which is only correct when both lists are sorted by `lo`. Input `a` (`group.ranges`) is guaranteed sorted and disjoint — `mergeFontSubsetSpecs` → `textToRanges` → `mergeRanges` (which `toSorted`s and coalesces), and the `FontSubsetGroup.ranges` doc comment says so. Input `b` (`faceRanges`, fontSubset.ts:63) comes straight from `parseCss` → `readFontFace` → `readUnicodeRanges` (cssAst.ts:164-169), which is a bare `filter().map().filter()` over `value.children` — it preserves CSS source order and never sorts or merges. I grepped every `unicodeRanges` reference in the package: the only other consumer is `cssFontAssets.ts:186`, which uses order-independent `.some()`, and the sibling dev-check path `rangesByFamily` (fontImportAttributes.ts:248-259) *does* call `mergeRanges` first — so the omission at fontSubset.ts:64 is an inconsistency, not an invariant held elsewhere. I hand-traced the stated counterexample: with `a = [{0x41,0x41}]` and `b = [{0x2000,0x206F},{0x20,0x7F}]`, the first iteration computes lo=0x2000 > hi=0x41 (no push), then `a[0].hi < b[0].hi` advances `i` past the end — result `[]`. `kept.length === 0` then hits fontSubset.ts:65-68, which `edits.remove(face.start, face.end)`s the whole `@font-face` and only bumps `droppedFaces`. The silence is confirmed at ComponentRegistry.ts:2272-2303: the per-variant `logger.info` loop never fires (no variants), `droppedFaces > 0` sets `subsetOutcome = 'applied'` (line 2289-2291), which suppresses the only warning (line 2299), and `droppedFaces` is logged nowhere — so the build stays green while the font vanishes from the page. Partial under-reporting is the worse sibling case: the face survives with a subset built from too few codepoints. The CSS spec places no ordering requirement on `unicode-range`, so this is legal input; it is invisible to the suite because every fixture is ascending (fontSubset.test.ts:17 `U+0000-00FF,U+0131,U+0152-0153`; :95 `U+0400-045F`; cssFontSubset.test.ts:21,29), as is @fontsource/Google Fonts output. That makes it a genuine latent bug with an unusual-but-legal trigger — BUG is correct. The proposed fix is sound: `mergeRanges` copies (`merged.push({...range})`) so it won't mutate the parsed AST.

Two of the three required legs check out; the third cannot be settled from source. (1) The ordering defect is real as written: `importUnique` (freshImport.ts:19-28) reads `prev`, `await`s its deletion, records `lastArtifact`, and only then issues `import(unique)` — so the delete is sequenced *before* the import, contradicting the header comment's claim that the lingering copy is 'the one the just-issued import still holds open'. For strictly sequential calls the behaviour is safe (`prev`'s import resolved in an earlier completed call); under concurrency `prev` can be an artifact whose import is still in flight. (2) The concurrency is reachable, and more easily than the finding claims. `compileAll` (ComponentRegistry.ts:724-731) computes `todo` synchronously from `!this.compiledComponents.has(f)` with no in-flight map; the only serialization primitive in the class is `serializeCssBundling`/`importedCssBatches` (lines 464-465, 2144), which covers CSS bundling only. Server-island components are never added to `ssrEntrypoints` (Mochi.ts:676-697) — `allServerIslands` only populates the name→path map at line 1237-1238 — so `/_mochi/island/:name` genuinely cold-compiles in dev (Mochi.ts:1612). `ServerIsland.ts`'s `_inflight` guard is per-element, so N wrappers for the same component fire N parallel fetches; `packages/site/src/demos/is-hydratable/IsHydratable.svelte:33,41` renders `HydrationProbe` twice in one page, which is exactly that shape. Entry naming (`'[name]-[hash].server.js'`, line 1010) is deterministic, so both passes land on the identical `outPath` and therefore the identical `lastArtifact` key. (3) What I cannot verify is the necessary condition for an observable failure: that Bun's `import()` yields to the *event loop* between being issued and reading the artifact. Call A issues `import(url_A)` in the same synchronous block as `lastArtifact.set`, so there is no gap before the import starts; call B can only delete `url_A` from a write-completion macrotask. If Bun's module fetch hook reads an on-disk file synchronously (which is my reading of its loader, and the entry's deps — content-hashed chunks and external `svelte/*` — are typically already in the process module cache), A's whole graph links across microtasks inside one macrotask and B can never interleave, making the race unobservable. If any hop does real async I/O, A fails with `Cannot find module` as described. The static-analysis-only constraint rules out the one-line probe that would decide this, and there is no concurrency test (freshImport.test.ts is purely sequential) or observed report in the repo. Worth noting separately: the same missing dedup creates a timing-independent hazard the finding does not flag — two concurrent `Bun.build`s write the same `outdir` filename, so `Bun.write(dest, Bun.file(outPath))` can copy a half-rewritten entry. Dev-only either way (production takes the plain `import()` branch at line 1094), and the recommended fix (import first, delete after; or an in-flight map on `compileAll`) is cheap and correct regardless of which way the timing falls.

Every link in this chain is confirmed in source. `setupTailwind` (tailwind.ts:90) hardcodes `mochiEvents.setHandler('tailwind-rebuild', 'file:change', …)` with a name that does not depend on `opts`. The emitter's `setHandler` (events.ts:498-509) looks up `byName.get(name)` and calls `base.off(prior.type, prior.handler)` before re-registering — exactly the eviction described — and its own docstring (lines 479-484) warns to namespace the name 'since two callers picking the same name silently evict each other'. So a second `setupTailwind` call removes the first call's `file:change` subscriber. The first stylesheet still gets its one-shot `compileTailwind(opts)` at line 67, then goes permanently stale with no error and no warning; since `compileTailwind` is exported separately for the no-watcher case, the watcher is the only reason to call `setupTailwind` at all. The framework's own convention confirms the intended shape: `ImageCache` builds a per-instance `mochi-image:cache-delete:${++cascadeSeq}` (imageCache.ts:130,182) and releases it via `removeHandler` in `dispose()` (line 196). `setupTailwind` returns `void` with no disposer, and I grepped Mochi.ts and devWatcher.ts for `mochiEvents.off` / `all.clear()` / `removeHandler` — none exist, so the handler and its captured `opts` do outlive teardown. The no-security-impact reasoning also holds: `file:change` is emitted only at devWatcher.ts:750, and `startDevWatcher` is gated behind `if (development)` at Mochi.ts:2151. Two caveats that weaken the argument without changing the verdict. First, the cited doc line (175-tailwind.md:159, 'scope your Tailwind CSS to a single page') is about which page imports the generated stylesheet, not about calling `setupTailwind` twice — the docs only ever show one call — so the 'docs nudge toward multiple scoped stylesheets' framing is a stretch. The stronger evidence is the real call site: `packages/demos/src/todo/routes.ts:8-15` mounts Tailwind from a per-feature route module, a pattern that silently breaks the moment a second feature folder copies it. Second, the finding's alternative fix (a module-level `++tailwindSeq` counter) is wrong — it would reintroduce handler stacking across the dev entry re-import that the hardcoded name exists to collapse (see the line-64 docstring and `freshImport(entryPath)` in cli/extractServeOptions.ts:87). Only the primary suggestion, deriving the name from `outputAbs`, satisfies both constraints.
